Class TestCompiler

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.processing.testing.TestCompiler
public final class TestCompiler extends Object
Compiles in-memory sources with the system Java compiler, in process, running the given annotation processors. 
Compilation compilation = TestCompiler.javac()
        .withProcessors(new MyProcessor())
        .withOptions("-Xlint:all,-processing", "-Werror")
        .compile(TestCompiler.source("example.Foo", """
                package example;
                class Foo {}
                """));

The sources are compiled against the class path and the module path of the running JVM, unless the options give a module path of their own. Sources outside a module read every module of that path; sources that include a module-info.java read what it requires. Generated sources, class files and resources are written to temporary directories, read back into the Compilation, and the directories are deleted.

A TestCompiler is immutable: withProcessors(Processor...) and withOptions(String...) return a new one.

    • withOptions

      public TestCompiler withOptions(String... options)
      Returns a compiler that passes options to javac, instead of the options this one passes. They come after -proc:full, which is always passed.

      To check that generated code compiles cleanly, use withOptions("-Xlint:all,-processing", "-Werror"): the processing lint warns whenever a processor does not claim its annotations, which well-behaved processors never do.

      javac checks the options when compile(List) runs: telling an option from the argument of another takes its file manager.

      Parameters:
      options - the javac options
      Returns:
      a compiler passing options

    • compile

      public Compilation compile(JavaFileObject... sources)
      Compiles sources.
      Parameters:
      sources - the compilation units, such as the ones source(String, String) returns
      Returns:
      the outcome; a compilation error is reported in it, not thrown
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if sources is empty or holds a file that is not a source file, or if javac rejects an option: unknown, without its argument, or with an invalid value
      IllegalStateException - if the running Java has no system compiler, or if javac finds options that cannot be used together
      RuntimeException - if an annotation processor, or a file given to javac, throws an exception, which is the cause of the one thrown
      UncheckedIOException - if the temporary output directories cannot be written, read or deleted
